# Data-Driven Gearing over Hand-Tuned RPM Bands

**Decision.** Choose gears from the car's **own engine data** — parsed out of the TORCS car XML —
rather than from tuned rpm thresholds or from a learned reward term.

**Date.** Shipped in `car_spec.py`, published 2026-07-10. Third and final answer in a documented
three-branch progression that began 2026-05-02.

## Two alternatives were tried first, and both are recorded

`INDEX.md` names the lineage outright:

> "**Gear ideas:** [gear_strategy_max_jerk] (raw jerk) → [headless] (rpm band) → [a.bhuiyan]
> (data-driven torque/shift map)."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/INDEX.md, 2026-07-10

**Attempt 1 — learn it from a jerk reward** (`gear_strategy_max_jerk`, tip 2026-05-02). Gear moved
into the action space and the reward paid for rising acceleration, on the theory that a good upshift
produces an acceleration spike. Its own report names the flaw: the only acceleration signal available
is the difference of successive `speedX` readings off the UDP sensor, so **the jerk estimate is
noisy**, and `jerk_threshold = 1` was "a coarse first guess". The branch stopped at WIP.

**Attempt 2 — hand-tuned rpm band** (`headless`). A reward paying 1.0 inside a 17k–19k rpm "optimum
band", tapering outside it, scaled by gear number. It worked well enough to become the branch's
headline feature, and `calculate_jerk_reward` was commented out in its favour — attempt 1 superseded
in place. But the constants are guesses fitted to one car:

> "Compared to the data-driven engine model in `[[a.bhuiyan]]` (`car_spec.py` parses the real torque
> curve), headless's rpm bands are hand-tuned constants."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/docs/branch-reports/headless.md, 2026-07-10

*(The `[[a.bhuiyan]]` in that line is an Obsidian wikilink in the source report, escaped here so it
does not resolve inside this wiki. It refers to the branch, not to a page.)*

That is the rejected alternative stated by the repo itself, in the repo's own words, in the report
for the branch that used it.

## What shipped instead

> "Data-driven car model for TORCS — every number comes from the car's own XML. No hardcoded
> driveline."
> — IT Applications in Business and Commerce/project/code/a.bhuiyan/gym_torcs/car_spec.py, 2026-07-10

`car_spec.py` (247 lines) resolves `practice.xml` → `scr_server.xml` → the car XML and extracts gear
ratios, gear efficiencies, final drive, rear-tyre radius, the rpm→N·m torque curve and the rev
limiter. `optimal_gear(speed)` then returns **the gear that maximises wheel tractive force right
now**, shifting at `DEFAULT_SHIFT_FRAC = 0.93` of the limiter. The module's own framing is that this
behaves "like a real ECU's shift map" and self-adapts to whatever car is configured.

It is the same technique as [[parse-track-xml-not-ttrackseg]] applied to the vehicle instead of the
circuit: read the simulator's configuration rather than guess at its runtime behaviour.

## Why this ordering matters

The gearbox stopped being something the agent had to learn. Under
[[residual-reinforcement-learning]] the deterministic baseline handles gears from the shift map, and
PPO only learns a bounded correction on top — so a whole class of [[reward-shaping]] term
(jerk bonuses, rpm-band bonuses) disappears from the objective. Fewer shaped terms is fewer ways for
the policy to find a degenerate optimum.

`car_spec.py` also **fails loud** rather than substituting defaults, so a caller that cannot resolve
the car XML falls back deliberately instead of silently driving on invented ratios.

## Costs and gaps

- Three branches spent on one subsystem. The gearing thread is named in `INDEX.md`'s
  "recurring findings" as a persistent problem across the whole team — see [[branch-per-experiment]].
- Only the `a.bhuiyan` tree gets the shift map; the shipped `stable` agent keeps speed-based
  auto-gear. Two of the repo's own code trees therefore disagree about gearing, and the repo does
  not reconcile them.

- **TODO:** whether `DEFAULT_SHIFT_FRAC = 0.93` was derived from the torque curve or chosen by feel
  is unrecorded, and the interview did not cover it. `confidence: low` on that constant specifically.
  Every other number in the module is parsed, not chosen.
